title: Geo-tier routing orchestrator with proactive cache-warmth auditor
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Implement a geo-aware routing orchestrator that enforces tier routing (hosted/dedicated/private) while proactively validating and warming KV/prefix caches in warm-standby regions. The feature couples a routing decision engine with a lightweight cache-warmth auditor that simulates a small set of representative traffic to keep per-model KV caches primed && validate fallback model variants for compatibility.

Motivation: Existing warm-standby flows rely on passive priming (user traffic or full-scale priming jobs) which leads to unpredictable cold-start latency and occasional model-variant incompatibilities during cutover. This ticket introduces an always-on, policy-driven auditor that: (1) scores readiness across region-tier-model combinations, (2) surfaces readiness scores to Console and routing policies, and (3) triggers controlled pre-warm probes to bring critical caches to an SLO-aligned warmth threshold prior to cutover.

Scope:
- Routing orchestrator: policy evaluation (latency budget, cost delta, regional capacity, customer tier), model variant compatibility table, and fallback selection rules.
- Cache-warmth auditor: executable probe runner that issues small inference prefixes across representative prompt bundles, tracks per-model KV/cache hit ratios, average token generation latency, and tokenized context fill rates.
- Readiness scoring: combine probe signals with capacity & infra health to produce a single readiness score (0-100) per region-tier-model variant.
- Integrations: Console readiness dashboard, alerting hooks (PagerDuty), rollout gating API for canary/cutover flows.

Out-of-scope: large-scale bulk pre-warming jobs, model re-training, or changes to the runtime kernel selection logic (will be handled via separate runtime optimizations tickets).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Routing orchestrator enforces policy decisions and can route requests using tier priorities (hosted -> dedicated -> private) and regional fallback according to configured latency budgets.
2) Auditor runs periodic probes for configured model variants and reports cache-warmth metrics into MetricsDB.
3) Readiness score is computed and available via a REST API AND shown in Console under 'Region Readiness'.
4) Cutover API rejects activation if readiness < 70 for target region unless override is granted with audit log.
5) Automated smoke test demonstrates successful failover with <25% added latency compared to baseline in a staged environment.
6) Documentation (Confluence) + runbook + PagerDuty escalation for readiness regressions created.
implementation_notes:
Planned components:
- routing-controller service (Go): evaluate policies, consult readiness API, select model variant/fallback, log decision rationale.
- auditor worker (Python): configurable probe sets per customer cohort, adaptive probe frequency based on traffic, token-limited to control cost.
- readiness-store (Timescale): store probe results, cache metrics, compute rollup scores.
- Console wire: new Region Readiness panel + per-model variant drilldown + historical probe timeline.
- Feature flags: enable per-customer and per-region.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive pre-warm probes reduce cold-start but increase cost; solution: adaptive frequency tied to SLA and customer tier.
- Strong gating (high readiness threshold) increases safety but slows failovers; allow override with audit trail for emergencies.
- Embedding readiness into routing adds latency to decision path; mitigate with local cache of readiness scores updated on 30s cadence.

Open implementation decisions:
- Final readiness aggregation formula (weighted: probe hit-rate 50%, latency delta 30%, infra health 20%).
- Probe payload selection algorithm: uniform sample vs. percentile-based prompt bundles.
risks:
- Probing may accidentally bias model caches causing skewed production metrics if probe prompts overlap with customer data. Mitigation: use synthetic/unrelated probe prompts and throttle per model.
- Cost blowup for high-cardinality model variants/regions. Mitigation: require policy to opt into 'continuous' warmth; default to on-demand pre-warm only for critical models.
- False positives/negatives in readiness score leading to unnecessary cutovers or blocked failovers. Mitigation: staged rollout and canary testing; maintain fallback to last-known-good region.
- Security: probes must not leak keys or customer data. Auditor will run with restricted IAM and isolated logging.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for routing decision logic and readiness API.
- Integration tests: simulate region failover in staging with service mesh; validate auditor warms KV cache and readiness score increases.
- Load test: create synthetic traffic to emulate 5 p95/p99 workloads while probing to ensure overhead <5% token cost.
- Chaos test: kill regional serving instances to ensure orchestrator falls back cleanly and readiness API reflects down-state.
- Smoke failover runbook executed during a maintenance window with operator observing metrics and fallback path.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged deploy to internal staging. Run automated integration + load tests (2 weeks).
2) Canary in 'eu-west-1' on low-traffic customers with continuous auditing on (4 days).
3) Expand to additional regions and customer tiers progressively, monitor Console readiness and incidents.
4) Full enablement with default thresholds after 4 successful canaries.
5) Postmortem and metrics review after 30 days to tune probe frequency and thresholds.
